topics.topic_label: Content provenance & training-data copyright (the Landgericht Munchen I enjoins Suno at GEMA's suit and the prohibition reaches use of protected works in training, not only generated output — the 'it's only parameters', US fair use and jurisdiction defences all failed; Article 50 provenance duties bite on 2 August and Google pulled its Earth AI image generator 48 hours before they did)

EU AI Act (Article 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 August across four cases — direct interaction, AI-generated content, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation, deepfakes and public-interest text — binding deployers as well as providers, carrying fines to EUR 15M or 3% of worldwide turnover, and explicitly not delayed by the omnibus; Commission enforcement powers activate the same day)

Content provenance & copyright (CAITA is operative at $5,000 per violation per day with licence revocation in 96 hours; Lawfare grants the doctrinal question and asks the administrative one — if human attribution is the line, someone must sort human from machine text at scale and no tool can; an e-commerce study finds the mandatory AI label damages even genuine photographs)

Content provenance & copyright (~190 organisations signed the transparency Code of Practice, 83 to Section 1 and 152 to Section 2, so the marking format gets settled in September task forces rather than in national court; on HN the argument has moved from 'is AI art good' to whether publishing it signals you are wasting the reader's time, with explicit calls for social enforcement)

Content provenance & copyright (Article 50 is being enforced since 2 August — chatbots must disclose, deepfakes must be labelled, generated content must carry machine-readable marks — and the two best pieces of the day both separate human-facing disclosure from machine-verifiable provenance instead of collapsing them into 'label your AI'; on HN the reader-side enforcement is already running, with AI hero images read as a costly-signalling failure at 772 points)

Content provenance & copyright (Article 50 went live on 2 August so AI-generated or manipulated content must carry machine-readable labels - and on the same front page TIME is caught serving AI crawlers a different site with advertising embedded in the text models ingest, Meta ran ads containing AI-generated CSAM, and Grokipedia is found to have silently stopped reviewing edits in April while still presenting as live)
